claude.sample_unit: patients (hospital external validation cohort; 375 in held-out test set)

links.outcome: Change in AUPRC and Brier score after fine-tuning synthetic-pretrained models on local hospital data versus zero-shot
links.effect: Domain adaptation improved AUPRC in 8/12 combinations (4 significant; best ΔAUPRC +0.1474, P<.001) and Brier in 11/12; zero-shot reduced AUPRC in most settings.
links.quote: The domain adaptation model showed ΔAUPRC>0 in 8 out of 12 combinations, with significant improvement over the baseline model observed in 4 combinations.

links.outcome: Distribution differences between synthetic development data and local hospital population
links.effect: Statistically significant differences for all variables (P<.05); adenocarcinoma 97.2% vs 55.6%; perineural invasion 29.4% vs 0.7%; zero-shot models degraded performance.
links.quote: A clear domain shift was observed between synthetic and hospital data, necessitating the use of domain adaptation techniques to ensure model performance in real-world settings.

links.outcome: Zero-shot performance of synthetic-trained models on local hospital data versus hospital-only baseline
links.effect: Zero-shot only 2 of 12 combinations had ΔAUPRC>0, none significant; 3 significantly degraded; AUPRC 0.2706-0.4171 vs baseline 0.3576-0.4663.
links.quote: Only 2 of 12 combinations exhibited ΔAUPRC>0, and none of these improvements were statistically significant.

unlisted_practices: Using synthetic data for pretraining predictive models with local fine-tuning (domain adaptation) as a privacy-preserving development strategy

links.effect: All variables differed (P<.05); adenocarcinoma 97.2% vs 55.6%, perineural invasion 29.4% vs 0.7%, vascular invasion 19.2% vs 9.4%.
links.quote: The prevalence of adenocarcinoma (histology) was significantly higher in the hospital data than in the synthetic data (97.2% vs 55.6%, P <.001), and perineural invasion (29.4% vs 0.7%, P <.001) and vascular invasion (19.2% vs 9.4%, P <.001) were higher in hospital data.

links.effect: Only 2/12 zero-shot combinations had ΔAUPRC>0; none were statistically significant.
links.quote: Only 2 of 12 combinations exhibited ΔAUPRC>0, and none of these improvements were statistically significant.

links.effect: ΔAUPRC>0 in 8/12 combinations; 4 statistically significant improvements over baseline.
links.quote: The domain adaptation model showed ΔAUPRC>0 in 8 out of 12 combinations, with significant improvement over the baseline model observed in 4 combinations.

links.effect: 10/12 zero-shot combinations showed no improvement, including 3 statistically significant degradations.
links.quote: The remaining 10 combinations showed no improvement, including 3 with statistically significant degradation.

links.outcome: colorectal cancer survival prediction AUPRC and calibration
links.effect: Domain adaptation improved AUPRC in 8/12 combinations (4 significant; best ΔAUPRC=+0.1474, P<.001) and improved Brier scores in 11/12 combinations (8 significant) over hospital baseline, outperforming zero-shot transfer.
links.quote: In contrast, the domain adaptation model improved AUPRC in 8/12 combinations, with 4 statistically significant gains; the best setting (XGBoost+RUS+F1 optimization) achieved AUPRC=0.5391 (Δ+0.1474; P<.001).
